messages:
Diego (oncall): incident-bot just paged — kv block-manager memory in prod-eu-1 up ~3.5x over baseline, tail latency climbing. Seeing continuous batching rate spike after the 03:40 deploy.
Maya Li: on it. which deploy? can we roll back the batching flag?
Diego (oncall): Jordan rolled out batch_window=30ms -> 10ms in the runtime config at 03:38. metric: continuous_batches/sec jumped x6.
Ben Kapoor: linking relevant dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/kv/blocks?orgId=1&var-region=eu-1
Alice Tran: customer alerts starting to come in for inference timeouts (>5s) on small-text models. Carlos, do we have customer-facing list?
Carlos (cust-succ): got two tickets from Acme and BrightPath—both on EU region. Escalated to SEs, they want ETA.
Jordan (runtime): re: deploy — I lowered batching to reduce latency for small requests, but didn't account for blockmgr compaction cost. my bad.
Maya Li: immediate plan: 1) throttle continuous batching rate 2) adjust block_size_target back to previous value 3) temporary canary rollback if needed.
Diego (oncall): rolling throttle now via feature-flag: `kv.batch.max_continuous_requests=200` -> set to 60. running: `curl -X POST https://config.redwood/api/flags -d '{"kv.batch.max_continuous_requests":60}'`
incident-bot: Flag change queued, propagating to region eu-1 (3 nodes).
Ben Kapoor: watch metrics: batches/sec, blockmgr.mem, tail-99 latency, and eviction rate.
Jordan (runtime): patch for block_size_target revert ready:
```
# revert block target to 64MB
block_manager:
  block_size_target_mb: 64
  eviction_policy: lru-prioritize-age
```
Maya Li: Diego — can you apply revert to the EU-1 canary first?
Diego (oncall): applying to canary (node eu1-canary-02) now: `kubectl apply -f revert-blocksize-canary.yaml`
Alice Tran: rolling logs show compaction spikes ~04:05: `blockmgr.compact_ms=12000` vs baseline 200ms. compaction triggered when fragmentation > 70%.
Ben Kapoor: compaction pause explains tail latency. if we reduce batching and increase block size, fragmentation window narrows.
Carlos (cust-succ): told Acme support we'll have an update in 30m and a mitigation ETA of 1h.
Maya Li: can we also temporarily disable background compaction on the canary to stop long tail? set `blockmgr.compaction.enabled=false` for canary only.
Jordan (runtime): doing that now for canary. command: `configctl set eu-1 canary blockmgr.compaction.enabled false`
incident-bot: config applied to eu1-canary-02.
Diego (oncall): canary metrics: batches/sec down 65%, blockmgr.mem stable, p99 latency down from 2.8s -> 550ms.
Maya Li: good. Plan after canary success: stage region eu-1 rollout with batching throttle + block_size revert, monitor 15m, then re-enable compaction with adjusted thresholds.
Ben Kapoor: I will add a temporary alert suppressor for noisy eviction alerts while we stabilize so the oncall noise is manageable.
Alice Tran: saved a small diagnostic bundle and heap histograms: s3://logs/prod/eu-1/blockmgr-diff-2765412345.tar.gz
Jordan (runtime): deploying staged rollout in 3 waves: canary (1 node) -> small pool (5 nodes) -> full region. each wave waits 15m gating on p99 and compaction_ms.
Diego (oncall): handoff: I'm going offline at 05:20 UTC. Maya you're taking primary oncall after I drop. leaving runbook: revert flag if p99 exceeds 1.2s for >10m; otherwise continue rollout.
Maya Li: acknowledged. I'll coordinate with Carlos for customer comms. tagging @here: if things degrade after handoff, page me.
Carlos (cust-succ): updated Acme/BrightPath: mitigation in progress, ETA ~45m.
Ben Kapoor: post-mortem notes starter: observed root cause = aggressive batching window change leading to compaction amplification + smaller block_size_target exposing fragmentation. action items: 1) gating/better perf tests for batching changes 2) config guardrails on blockmgr params 3) compaction throttle feature 4) customer incident follow-up.
Alice Tran: also add a telemetry spike detector for compaction_ms to warn before alerts trigger.
Maya Li: final status at 05:10 UTC before handoff: EU-1 region stabilized on staged rollout, p99 within SLAs, no new customer pages. leaving the thread for follow-up.
Diego (oncall): thanks team — handing off. good notes in runbook.
incident-bot: Thread marked acknowledged and assigned to Maya Li for follow-up.
Maya Li: I'll open the postmortem ticket and assign owners. thanks all for fast ops.
